name: 40651-specdecode-qwen38b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1: one engine on one GPU, with the speculator head co-resident.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=64, bounded at 4000 requests / 1800 s safety, with a 10% warmup and a 10% cooldown taken by request count.
workload: guidellm `json_file` over `configs/data/mtbench-4000-qwen3.jsonl`, single turn, no prefix: 4000 rows drawn with replacement under a fixed seed from the 80 first-turn questions of `philschmid/mt-bench` (realised prompt mean 67.692 tokens, p50 38, p90 199, max 356), regenerable with `configs/data/make-dataset.py`. Output is exactly 128 tokens on every row (`ignore_eos: true`); `request_format: plain` posts raw text to the completions path with no chat template; every request is sampled at temperature 1.0 with top_p 1.0 and top_k 0.
purpose: An eight-billion-parameter chat assistant answering short open-ended questions with 128-token replies for 64 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. Nothing here was searched for; there is no tunable.yaml.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
data-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# num_speculative_tokens 7 OVERRIDES the head's own packaged default of 3.
speculative-config: {"method": "eagle3", "model": "RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens": 7}

# The longest request in the request file is 356 prompt + 128 output tokens, so neither
# max-model-len nor max-num-batched-tokens binds, and max-num-seqs is twice the 64 streams
# scenario.json offers so the scheduler never limits concurrency. gpu-memory-utilization is this
# engine's own default, written down so it cannot drift.
max-model-len: 2048
max-num-seqs: 128
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9

# Off deliberately: the 4000 requests are drawn from 80 distinct questions, so with the cache on
# most would skip prefill entirely and this would stop being the declared workload.
enable-prefix-caching: false
